???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What is the 8-bit unit that files and memory are stored in called?"

        A byte. It holds one of 256 values, and one character may need several bytes.

        Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

    ??? question "Which agreement between caller and callee says where arguments are placed and where the return value is found?"

        The calling convention.

        Introduced in [7. Functions and control flow](stage-7-functions-and-control-flow.md).

    ??? question "Which v0.1 type holds a fixed number of values of one type, with sizes known at compile time, such as `[f32; 4]`?"

        A fixed-size array. Its element type and every dimension are part of its type.

        Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#71-array-types).

    ??? question "What is one size in an array type such as `[f32; 4, 8]` called, and when must it be known?"

        A dimension. Each one must evaluate at compile time to an integer that fits `usize`.

        Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#72-dimension-rules).

    ??? question "What do you declare to group related values into a new named type, such as `Point` with `x` and `y`?"

        A struct. Declaring it creates a type; a struct expression creates a value of that type.

        Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../../specification/structs.md#81-declaration).
